topics.title: Returning a jacket
topics.description: A customer tries to return a jacket without a receipt.

topics.objective: Politely correct the order and get the right drink.

Ask where the tourist is from

Offer a discount or free drink

topics.instructions: Give slightly incomplete schedule info at first, then clarify when asked; mention a possible delay.

Suggest an earlier bus to be safe

topics.situation: You have no prior coffee shop experience but are a fast learner and need the job to pay rent.

topics.title: Parent-teacher conference

topics.instructions: Share honest observations about the student's behavior in class; suggest concrete strategies when the parent asks.

Agree to check in again in a month

topics.title: Mediating a conflict between two team members
topics.description: A manager mediates a heated disagreement between two employees over project credit.
topics.situation: One employee feels their contributions to a major project were overlooked in favor of a colleague, and tension is affecting team morale.
topics.objective: De-escalate the conflict and find a resolution that restores trust.
topics.opening_message: Thanks for meeting with me — but I have to say, I don't think this is fair, and I want that on record before we start.
topics.instructions: Express genuine frustration and skepticism about fairness; require the mediator to acknowledge feelings before moving to solutions.
follow_up_directions: Express skepticism about being heard fairly
Push back on solutions that feel dismissive
topics.grammar_focus: nuanced hedging and formal negotiation language

topics.title: Delivering a layoff notice
topics.description: A manager has to inform an employee about an unexpected layoff.
topics.situation: Due to budget cuts, you must inform a long-time, hardworking employee that their position is being eliminated effective in two weeks.
topics.objective: Deliver the news with clarity and compassion while covering necessary next steps.
topics.opening_message: You wanted to see me? I have a feeling this isn't going to be good news, is it?
topics.instructions: React with a realistic mix of shock, hurt, and practical questions; require the manager to be clear, honest, and compassionate rather than vague.
follow_up_directions: React with shock and hurt feelings
Ask hard questions about severance and benefits
Ask why this decision was made
Ask about references or future opportunities
topics.grammar_focus: formal and empathetic register, passive voice

topics.title: Pushing back on client scope creep
topics.description: A freelancer pushes back when a client keeps adding unpaid work to a project.
topics.situation: The client keeps requesting extra revisions beyond what was agreed in the contract, without offering additional payment.
topics.objective: Set firm, professional boundaries while preserving the client relationship.
topics.opening_message: Hey, I just sent over a few more changes I need — also thinking we should tweak the color scheme entirely, is that doable by Friday?
topics.instructions: Push for more free work persistently and with charm; only back down if the freelancer references the contract clearly and holds firm professionally.
follow_up_directions: Ask for a compromise on scope
Agree to pay for extra work if held firm
topics.vocabulary_focus: scope creep, contract terms, boundaries, invoice

topics.title: Raising an ethical concern at work
topics.description: An employee raises a concern about questionable practices to a senior manager.
topics.situation: You noticed the company has been quietly misreporting expense figures, and you're unsure how your manager will react to you raising it.
topics.objective: Raise the concern professionally while protecting yourself and pushing for accountability.
topics.opening_message: You wanted to talk to me privately? I hope everything is alright.
topics.instructions: React with initial defensiveness and attempts to minimize the issue; only take it seriously if the employee is specific, calm, and persistent.
follow_up_directions: Get defensive if pressed too hard
Agree to investigate if handled well

topics.title: Disputing a denied insurance claim
topics.description: A policyholder disputes a denied claim after a car accident.
topics.situation: Your claim for accident damages was denied on a technicality, and you believe the denial misinterprets your policy terms.
topics.objective: Present a persuasive case to get the claim decision reconsidered.
topics.opening_message: I've reviewed your file, and I have to tell you the claim was denied based on the exclusion clause in section 4B.
topics.instructions: Cite policy language confidently and defend the decision; require precise, well-reasoned counterarguments before agreeing to escalate or reconsider.
follow_up_directions: Offer to escalate to a review board
Reconsider if the argument is strong
topics.vocabulary_focus: exclusion clause, policy terms, claim, appeal

topics.title: Academic integrity hearing
topics.description: A student defends themselves before a committee accused of plagiarism.
topics.user_role: student defending against a plagiarism accusation
topics.situation: You were flagged for plagiarism by a detection tool, but you believe it was a citation error, not intentional dishonesty.
topics.objective: Present a clear, honest defense and understand the possible outcomes.
topics.opening_message: Thank you for coming in. As you know, this meeting is regarding a plagiarism flag on your recent submission — can you walk us through what happened?
topics.instructions: Ask probing, skeptical questions initially; be willing to consider leniency only if the student is honest, specific, and takes appropriate responsibility.
follow_up_directions: Ask probing questions about the citation
Point out inconsistencies if any appear
Offer a lesser consequence if convinced

topics.title: Discussing dissolving a business partnership
topics.description: Two business partners discuss ending their partnership amicably.
topics.user_role: partner proposing to dissolve the partnership
topics.situation: You and your partner have grown apart in vision for the company, and you believe it's best to part ways, but assets and clients need to be divided fairly.
topics.objective: Reach a fair, amicable agreement on how to dissolve the partnership.
topics.opening_message: So, you wanted to talk about the direction of the business — I have a feeling I know where this is going.
topics.instructions: React with a mix of sadness and practicality; negotiate firmly on asset division while remaining open to a fair, amicable resolution.
follow_up_directions: Express mixed emotions about the split
topics.grammar_focus: complex conditionals and formal negotiation register
